academic_translation:
Knowing all sentient beings to be just as the self is,
Knowing all phenomena to be just as all sentient beings are,
Not conceptualizing either non-arising or arising—
This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
translation: You should know that all living beings are just like the self. Know that all things are just like all living beings. Do not think about arising or no arising. This is the practice of highest perfect wisdom.

academic_translation:
However many names of phenomena are proclaimed in the world,
Having abandoned arising and passing away regarding them all,
One attains the supreme, deathless primordial wisdom, beyond which there is no other;
Therefore, this is called the perfection of wisdom.
translation: People in the world have many names for things. But you must let go of their arising and passing away. Then you will gain the highest, deathless deep knowing. There is nothing greater than this. That is why it is called perfect wisdom.

academic_translation:
Any bodhisattva who practices in this way without doubt
Should be known as endowed with wisdom and abiding in equality;
Fully understanding that phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature,
This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.

locked_terms.use: with no nature of its own

translation: Any awakening hero who practices this way without doubt has true wisdom. You should know they rest in sameness. They completely understand that all things are with no nature of their own. This is the practice of highest perfect wisdom.

academic_translation: The second chapter, teaching the knowledge of all paths.
translation: The second chapter, teaching knowing all the paths.

academic_translation:
Whoever does not abide in form, does not abide in feeling,
Whoever does not abide in perception, does not abide in volition,
And whoever does not abide in consciousness, abides in the true nature of phenomena;
This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
translation: Whoever does not get stuck on form does not get stuck on feeling. They do not get stuck on any idea or intention. Whoever does not get stuck on awareness rests in the true nature of things. This is the practice of perfect wisdom, the highest perfection.

academic_translation:
One does not abide in the permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant,
Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness;
One does not abide in attaining the fruit, nor in the stage of an arhat,
And one does not abide in the stage of a pratyekabuddha, nor likewise the stage of a Buddha.
translation: You do not hold onto what is lasting or always changing. You do not hold onto happiness or suffering, or what is nice or not nice. You do not hold onto a self or no self. You do not hold onto the way things really are, or emptiness. You do not hold onto getting the fruit. You do not hold onto the level of a worthy one. You do not hold onto the level of a solitary Buddha, or even the level of a Buddha.

The Guide does not stay in the realm not made by causes. He also does not stay in things made by causes. He practices by not staying anywhere. In the same way, an awakening hero rests on a base through a stay without staying. The Victorious One taught that a stay without staying is the true way to stay.

academic_translation:
Those who think, "May I become a śrāvaka of the Sugata,"
Or wish to become a pratyekabuddha, and likewise a Dharma King, a Buddha,
Cannot attain them without relying on this patience,
Just as one sees no crossing to go from this shore to the other.
translation: Some people wish to be a listener of the Well-Gone One. Others wish to become a solitary Buddha. Some wish to be a King of the Teaching, a Buddha. But they cannot reach these goals without relying on this patience. It is like trying to cross a river without finding a way to the other shore.

academic_translation:
The teaching of the Dharma, the listening, and whatever is taught,
The attainment of the fruit, the pratyekabuddha, and likewise the Protector of the World,
And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the wise and lucid—
The Tathāgata has taught that all these are like an illusion.
translation: Think of the teaching, the listening, and what is taught. Think of getting the fruit. Think of the solitary Buddha and the Protector of the World. Think of the peace beyond sorrow reached by wise and clear minds. The Thus-Gone One taught that all these things are like an illusion.

academic_translation:
These four persons are not afraid of that:
The child of the Victors skilled in the truth, and the irreversible one,
The arhat who has cleared away stains and abandoned doubt,
And fourth, the one fully embraced by a spiritual friend.
translation: Four kinds of persons are not afraid of this. The first is a child of the Victorious Ones who is skilled in the truth. The second is someone who is never turning back. The third is a worthy one who has washed away dirt and dropped all doubt. The fourth is someone fully held by a wise friend.

A wise and smart awakening hero practices like this. They do not train in the level of a worthy one. They do not train in the level of a solitary Buddha. For the sake of knowing everything, they train following a Buddha's qualities. Whoever does not train in learning and not learning, that is real training.

academic_translation:
It is not for the sake of the increase, complete decrease, or complete apprehension of form;
Not training for the sake of completely apprehending various phenomena,
Yet training and completely apprehending omniscience itself—
Whatever definite emergence this is, it is the training of those who delight in qualities.
translation: They do not train to make form grow or shrink. They do not train to hold onto form. They do not train to hold onto different things. Still, they train and fully hold onto knowing everything. This sure way out is the training of those who love good qualities.

Form is not wisdom. There is no wisdom in form. Awareness, an idea, feeling, and intention are not wisdom. There is no wisdom in them, either. This is exactly like the element of space. There is no difference at all.

The nature of something to hold onto is boundless. Whatever the nature of living beings is, that is also boundless. The nature of the element of space is also boundless. The wisdom of the Knower of the World is boundless, too.

The Guide has clearly taught that an idea is this shore. By breaking down and leaving behind every idea, you cross to the far shore. Those who become free from any idea reach the far shore. They stay in the word of the Teacher.

academic_translation:
Even if the Teacher were to remain for as many eons
As there are grains of sand, and fully proclaim the word "sentient beings,"
Since they are pure from the beginning, how could sentient beings arise?
This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
translation: The Teacher could stay for as many ages as there are grains of sand. He could clearly say the words 'living beings.' But since they are pure from the very start, how could living beings ever arise? This is the practice of the highest perfection, perfect wisdom.

academic_translation:
When I spoke in conformity with this supreme perfection,
At that time the supreme being of the past
Said, "In a future time you will become a Buddha."
"I received the prophecy"—thus the Victor spoke.
translation: When I spoke the truth of this highest perfection, the highest being of the past spoke to me. He said, 'In the future, you will become a Buddha.' I received this prediction. This is what the Victorious One said.

academic_translation:
This perfection of wisdom in which the Protectors practice—
Whoever pays respect, retains, and fully understands its meaning,
Will not be harmed by poison, weapons, fire, or water,
And Māra and the factions of Māra will find no opportunity against them.
translation: The Protectors practice this perfect wisdom. This perfection keeps people safe. If anyone respects, remembers, and truly understands it, they will not be hurt by poison, weapons, fire, or water. Mara and Mara's side will never find a chance to harm them.

academic_translation:
If someone were to build stūpas of the seven precious things
For a Sugata who has passed into parinirvāṇa and make offerings,
And with those stūpas of the Sugata, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
Were to fill thousands of millions of fields,
translation: Imagine someone builds shrines out of the seven treasures. They build them for a Well-Gone One who has passed into the final peace beyond sorrow. They make offerings there. Imagine they build as many shrines as there are grains of sand in the Ganges river. Imagine these shrines fill thousands of millions of lands.

academic_translation:
By way of supposition, if in infinite millions of fields
All the sentient beings, however many reside there,
Doing no other work, with divine flowers, supreme incense, and
Ointments, were to make offerings at the three times of each day, for an eon or more—
translation: Imagine all the living beings in those endless millions of lands do no other work. Instead, they make offerings for an age or longer. They offer heavenly flowers, sweet incense, and oils in the past, present and future.

academic_translation:
Whoever, since from it the ten powers of the Guides will arise,
Writes this Mother of the Sugatas in a book,
Retains it, and pays reverence with flowers and ointments,
The merit of having built and made offerings to those stūpas does not match a fraction of it.
translation: The ten powers of the Guides will come from this wisdom. So, someone might write this Mother of the Well-Gone Ones in a book. They might keep it and honor it with flowers and sweet oils. If they do, they gain much more stored-up goodness. Building and making offerings to all those shrines does not even match a tiny part of it.

academic_translation:
This perfection of wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra of knowledge;
It pacifies the dharmas of sorrow and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings.
Whichever Protectors of the World are in the past, and whichever are in the ten directions,
Having trained in this mantra of knowledge, they became unsurpassed kings of physicians.
translation: The perfect wisdom of the Victorious Ones is a great spell of knowledge. These words of knowing calm the sadness and suffering in every realm of living beings. Every Protector of the World from the past and in the ten directions trained in this perfection. By learning it, each became a perfect doctor and an unsurpassed king of healers.

academic_translation:
Those who practice the conduct endowed with benefit and compassion,
The wise, having trained in this mantra of knowledge, touch awakening;
Whatever is conditioned happiness and unconditioned happiness,
One should know that all that happiness arises from this.
translation: Wise people act with benefit and compassion. They train in these words of knowing and touch awakening. There is happiness made by causes and happiness not made by causes. You should know that all that happiness comes from this.

Seeds planted in the earth will sprout. When the right conditions come together, many different shapes are born. The five perfections and all the good qualities of awakening are the same. All of them are born from perfect wisdom.

academic_translation:
Whichever path a universal monarch always travels,
On that very path, the seven precious things and all the military forces go;
Wherever this perfection of wisdom of the Victors goes,
Along that very path, all the qualities will go.
translation: Whenever a ruler of the whole world travels, the seven treasures and his army follow his path. Wherever the perfect wisdom of a Victorious One goes, every good quality also travels along that path. All these qualities follow this perfection of wisdom.

academic_translation:
Śakra, having been fully asked a question by the Victor, replied:
Even if there were Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
And all of those were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors,
I would take this very perfection of wisdom.
translation: A Victorious One asked Shakra a question, and Shakra replied. He said, 'Imagine there were as many Buddha-lands as grains of sand in the Ganges river. Even if they were all completely filled with the relics of Victorious Ones, I would still choose this perfect wisdom. I would take this very perfection of wisdom.'

academic_translation:
If asked why, it is not that I lack respect for the bodily relics;
However, because they are fully permeated by wisdom, they are worshipped.
For example, just as a person relying on a king obtains reverence,
The relics of a Buddha rely on the perfection of wisdom.
translation: If you ask why, it is not because I lack respect for a relic. People honor these relics because they are filled with wisdom. Think of a person who serves a king. People show them respect because they rely on the king. In the same way, a relic of a Buddha is respected because it relies on perfect wisdom. It relies on this perfection of wisdom.

A precious jewel has every good quality and is priceless. Whatever box it rests in deserves respect. Even if the jewel is taken out, people still take joy in the box. This is because those good qualities belong to that precious jewel.
